description: Figure 2 illustrates five different layer grouping patterns, comparing the relative number of layers across four sequential groups within each pattern. The horizontal axis serves as the category axis, displaying five distinct grouping configurations labeled from left to right as "Increasing," "Uniform," "Decreasing," "Spindle," and "Bottleneck." Within each of these five labeled configurations, there is a group of four adjacent bars representing the sequential groups (identified in the caption as $G_1$ through $G_4$) ordered from left to right. The vertical axis represents the number of layers in the groups; however, it lacks an explicit axis line, numerical labels, tick marks, or units, indicating a relative linear scale rather than absolute values. All bars across the figure are colored light green with black outlines. In the "Increasing" pattern, the four bars progressively increase in height from left to right, with the first bar being the shortest and the fourth being the tallest. The "Uniform" pattern consists of four bars of identical height. The "Decreasing" pattern features four bars that progressively decrease in height, starting with the tallest on the left and ending with the shortest on the right. The "Spindle" pattern displays shorter bars of equal height at the first and fourth positions, and taller bars of equal height at the second and third positions. Conversely, the "Bottleneck" pattern shows taller bars of equal height at the first and fourth positions, and shorter bars of equal height at the second and third positions. The bars are visually grouped by their respective pattern labels, and no specific bars are visually emphasized through shading or bolding beyond the standard light green fill and black outline.
